blocks.heading: Angles and lines
lines: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, around a point to 360°.
With parallel lines, alternate and corresponding angles are equal.
A triangle's angles add to 180°. An exterior angle equals the two opposite interior angles added.

blocks.heading: Triangles
lines: Area = ½ × base × height. Heron: √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)), with s half the perimeter.
Any two sides add up to more than the third.
Equilateral, side a: height (√3/2)a, area (√3/4)a².

blocks.heading: Similar triangles and bisectors
lines: Equal angles mean the sides are in one ratio k, and the areas in k².
A line parallel to one side cuts the other two sides in the same ratio.
The bisector of angle A splits BC in the ratio AB : AC.

blocks.heading: Circles
lines: Circumference 2πr, area πr².
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circle on the same arc. The angle in a semicircle is 90°.
A tangent is at 90° to the radius. Two tangents from one point are equal.
The perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord, so (half chord)² + distance² = r².
In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles add to 180°.

blocks.heading: Polygons
lines: Interior angles of an n-sided polygon add to (n − 2) × 180°.
Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 360° ÷ n.
Number of diagonals: n(n − 3) ÷ 2.
Regular hexagon, side a: six equilateral triangles, area (3√3/2)a².

blocks.heading: Coordinates
lines: Distance: √((x2 − x1)² + (y2 − y1)²).
Slope: (y2 − y1) ÷ (x2 − x1). Parallel lines have equal slopes; perpendicular slopes multiply to -1.
